topics.label: Introduction and framing of complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and sets expectations for the session.

topics.label: Foundational overview and nomenclature of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental concepts, general functions, and naming conventions of the complement system.

topics.label: Central role of C3 and activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how C3 functions as the central fulcrum and detail the three upstream pathways that trigger its activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream effector processes carried out by complement activation to destroy pathogens and stimulate immune responses.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct disease presentations and clinical outcomes resulting from genetic or secondary deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the evolutionary adaptations and mechanisms employed by pathogens to evade complement-mediated killing.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and provides a preview of the upcoming lecture topic.
